title: Demand Signal
description: One atomic record of a customer asking for a capability, from any source — solicitation, RFI, industry day, conference, one-on-one, trial, demo feedback, debrief, or partner conversation. The register (signals/demand-signals.jsonl) is append-only and workspace-global, not per-proposal: its purpose is to aggregate demand across the whole pipeline so the CTO shop sees frequency and weight rather than anecdotes. BD owns our_status; the CTO shop owns cto_disposition. The two are deliberately separate opinions and must never be merged — where they disagree is the agenda of the quarterly capability-demand review.

signal_id.description: Stable identifier, monotonically assigned. Never reused, never renumbered — briefs and CTO dispositions cite it.

date_observed.description: The date the customer said it, NOT the date it was transcribed. Verbal asks lead the RFP by 6-18 months; the observation date is what makes that lead time measurable.

source_type.description: Where the ask came from. Non-solicitation sources are first-class: they are earlier and usually less filtered than the written requirement.

source_ref.description: Auditable pointer back to the source. For proposals: 'proposals/<slug>/working/requirement-matrix.md#R3'. For notes: the path under inputs/06_notes/ or scrubs/. Every signal must be traceable to a document or a dated note, or engineering is right not to trust it.

customer.description: Agency or organization that made the ask (DIA, USSOCOM, Army FCC, NATO ACT).

program.description: Program, challenge, or effort name, when the ask is attached to one.

proposal_slug.description: The proposals/<slug>/ directory, when the signal came out of an active pursuit. Null for conference and relationship signals with no pursuit yet.

requirement.description: The ask in one sentence, in the customer's own words wherever possible. Verbatim customer language is the part engineering trusts; paraphrase loses it.

capability_theme.description: One theme from reference/capability-themes.md. This is the join key that turns 400 one-off requirements into a leaderboard. Adding a new theme is a deliberate edit to that file, not a free-text entry.

demand_strength.description: How hard the customer asked. mandatory-passfail = no bid without it. mandatory-scored = scored evaluation criterion. desired = stated preference or 'desired solution' language. curiosity = asked in conversation, not yet a requirement (the most valuable class for roadmap lead time).

rubric_weight_pct.description: Percentage weight of the scored criterion this ask maps to, when the solicitation publishes weights. Lets the brief rank by evaluated points rather than raw count.

pursuit_value_usd.description: Estimated value of the pursuit this signal came from, for dollar-weighted theme ranking. Sourced from HubSpot; null when unknown.

our_status.description: BD's read at the time of observation. 'shipping' = provable today with a ledger citation. 'prototype' = exists, not productized. 'roadmap' = BD believes it is planned. 'gap' = we could not answer the ask. 'no-plan' = gap with no known intent to close it. 'unknown' = extracted mechanically, not yet reviewed by a human.

bid_impact.description: What this ask cost us in the bid: prose we had to hedge, a teaming arrangement we had to make, criteria we scored low on, or a no-bid. The single most persuasive field in the register — 'the customer wanted X' is a wish, 'we hedged 3.2 and teamed it out' is a requirement.

evidence_id.description: The my-company/evidence-ledger.json item that proves this capability, once one exists. A capability that is real but absent from the ledger is invisible to the proposal pipeline, which means we do not get credit for it.

cto_disposition.description: The CTO shop's answer. Owned by engineering, transcribed by BD from the brief's disposition column. 'already-exists-ask-me' means BD and enablement have a communication problem, not engineering. 'wont-build' is a valid and useful answer: it tells BD to team for the theme instead of hedging, earlier.

cto_disposition_detail.description: Free text from engineering — target quarter for 'planned', what needs scoping, why not building, or which existing capability already covers it.

cto_disposition_date.description: When the disposition was given. Drives the median-age-of-undispositioned-gap metric and flags dispositions stale enough to re-ask.

cto_owner.description: Named individual in the CTO shop accountable for the disposition. A theme with no owner does not get closed.

notes.description: Anything that does not fit a field. Keep short.
